title: Krawtchouk polynomial
statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $j$, define a polynomial in $\mathbb{R}[X]$ by summing over $0\le k\le j$ the terms
\[(-1)^k\frac{(n)_{\underline{k}}}{k!}\,\frac{(n-X)_{\underline{j-k}}}{(j-k)!},\]
where $(y)_{\underline{m}}=y(y-1)\cdots(y-m+1)$ is the falling factorial and $(y)_{\underline{0}}=1$.
